ports.note: Every port a chart can draw, declared always, and none of them required. A chart draws what it is given, so which ports exist is not a question for the practitioner to answer before they have the shape -- the treatment map_output took on 2026-10-14 and table_output on 2026-10-27. `series` remains reachable only on a workflow saved with inputMode 'series'; a Cases by period table connected to `records` draws the same curve, because the shape that arrives decides and not the port it arrived on.

ontology.note: Existing ontology alignment; full configuration and port shape contracts remain to be defined.

changes.description: Declare its own shape into the write-up. Every run now machines a note into the Results section of the Notes tab stating what this artifact is made of. Experiment 147 measured that a Results section is mostly artifacts rather than prose, and until now not one artifact in this application could put a single word into a write-up: the figure was drawn, the receipt recorded what it drew, and the Notes tab had nothing from it. THE NOTE CARRIES NO NUMBER, which is the rule the whole change is shaped around -- experiment 141's amendment of 2026-10-30 settled that a figure's number is computed when a document is rendered, from the note's position in the IMRaD outline and the venue's own convention, because setting one figure aside for a venue moves every number after it. A note that wrote "Table 1" into its text would be right when machined and wrong the first time somebody dragged a card. The note is editable like any machined note: editing it forks it into a note of the author's own and the machined one goes on being rewritten by every run. It does not write over the caption a chart already states. `ChartSummary.caption` has existed since well before this change -- `rateChart` names the numerator, the multiplier, the denominator unit and the rate kind, and says when the vintages disagree -- and it reached no write-up, which is the same shape experiment 149 found for the example's own notes: produced, stored, never put in front of a reader. The note carries that line and adds the bar count, the category column and a statement that a bar at zero may be a withheld value rather than a measured zero, which `chart-output.ts` already names in its own comment as the thing that has to be said. THE CAPTION IS NOT MACHINED AND IS NOT CLAIMED. The practitioner, 2026-10-30: "Captions are the user's responsibility, unless there is a way to machine it based on table, map, chart or equation semantics." Everything in this note is read off a declaration, which is the exception that rule names; the caption itself states the subject, the population, the place and the period in the author's words and none of that is derivable here. The first version of this release called its output a caption and filed it under a function word invented for the purpose, which claimed an authorial act while delivering something else -- the same error experiment 149 settled for notes in general, arriving one level down. What would make a real caption machinable is 147's chain for the machined title -- design, place, outcome, period -- of which only place is declared today.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently. The self-description added in 0.8.0 is covered by tests/artifact-notes.test.mjs (13 unit checks, including that nothing machined numbers its own artifact or calls itself a caption, that an unnamed artifact is left unnamed rather than titled, and that a unit is stated once) and by tests/equation-notes.browser.mjs over the South London example on Chromium and WebKit. Both were mutation-checked by reintroducing the behaviour they forbid.

html.note: This project's own bars. Versioned by this release rather than by a library, and it emits no specification because it has none to give.
